transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Evan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Dylan Chen (Redwood Solutions), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Product); Maya Lopez (Aurora PM), Jamal Reed (Aurora Cloud Architect), Anika Bose (Aurora Marketplace Lead), Victor Kim (Aurora Security)

--- Optional auto-summary: agreed to create a formal reference architecture doc, Redwood to provide terraform + helm examples, Aurora to supply marketplace assets and security checklist. Plan integration benchmarks week of 12/27.

Topics: reference architecture, marketplace listing assets, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), KMS/encryption, benchmark plan, rollout and listing timeline

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Evan: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, so let's aim to cover the ref arch, marketplace tile requirements, and the integration test plan. Maya, you want to kick us off with Aurora's goals here?
[00:18] Maya: Yeah thanks Evan. For us it's two things: number one, make sure the marketplace listing is turnkey for our customers -- like they should be able to click deploy and not have to wire a bunch of things. Number two, joint reference arch that shows best practices for private deployments, VPC peering, KMS, etc. Lead gen is nice but first priority is low-friction install.
[00:40] Jamal: And to add, our enterprise customers are strict on key management -- they want BYOK/HSM options, audit logs, and SSO integration. So the ref arch needs to call those out.
[00:52] Priya: Yep TOTALLY. From Redwood's side we can support both Hosted API and Redwood Private (we sometimes call it Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicatd in notes) -- the reference arch should show both flows: hosted for quick dev/test and private for regulated customers. For private we recommend a control plane in Aurora VPC and customer-managed data plane or an on-prem bundle depending on the customer's preference.
[01:12] Anika: For marketplace listing, our product requirements are pretty standard -- logo, short/long description, 2 screenshots, optional video, and a one-click deploy template (terraform/helm). We also need icons in 512px and 1024px.
[01:25] Dylan: Good, we already have terraform examples for Dedicated and a helm chart for the private on-prem package. I'll standardize those into a single repo snippet. Small note: our helm chart expects the KV cache config to be optional; sometimes transcriptions in docs call it K V cache, but it's the kv-cache we use for prefix caching.
[01:45] Victor: On security -- audit logs, encryption at rest, and KMS integration are a must. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS across both hosted and private?
[01:55] Priya: Short answer yes for Private; for hosted we have a bring-your-own-key option in enterprise plans and can integrate with partner KMSs via our control plane. There are a few caveats around multi-tenant hosted offerings vs Dedicated. We'll surface that in the security checklist.
[02:12] Jamal: Networking question -- for VPC peering we usually do VPC peering + private IPs, or transit gateway. Any latency implications for inference if we peer across regions?
[02:25] Lena: Good question. Latency depends on model size and token throughput. For large LLMs we recommend colocating inference nodes in the same region to avoid cross-region hops. The ref arch will show an example where the inference cluster sits in the Aurora region and the control plane communicates over secure channels.
[02:42] Maya: Great. Regarding marketplace tile, timeline? We want to aim for listing by mid-January if possible.
[02:50] Evan: That seems doable. We should get assets from Anika this week, and Redwood will produce the ref arch draft within a week. Quick run through of owners?
[02:59] Anika: I'll get the logos and copy together. Quick question -- do you need any customer screenshots or can we use demo UI?
[03:08] Priya: Demo UI is fine for the tile, but for the ref arch docs we prefer a small benchmark screenshot from a perf test (latency/throughput) -- even synthetic data is OK to show numbers.
[03:20] Jamal: We'll also need a section on RBAC and SSO. Our customers use SAML or OIDC; is Redwood compatible?
[03:29] Priya: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC with SCIM provisioning is supported on enterprise plans and Private deployments. We'll include a sample SAML config.
[03:38] Dylan: One gotcha we should call out: model quantization and kernel selection can change perf numbers. If you pick a q4_0 or q8 model the throughput/latency changes; we'll include recommended quantization profiles by workload.
[03:52] Victor: For compliance we need SOC2 scope info and whether audit logs include token-level traces.
[03:58] Evan: We have SOC2 docs and our audit logs give token-level metadata (not raw content unless customer opts in), we'll share the compliance pack.
[04:08] Maya: Nice. Can we sketch the high-level ref arch now? Maybe Priya can walk through?
[04:15] Priya: Sure. High-level, two lanes: Hosted flow: Customer calls Redwood hosted API -> our hosted runtime -> model catalog -> responses. Private flow: Customer deploys Private control plane in Aurora VPC -> data plane lives in customer's VPC or on-prem -> KMS integration for keys -> optional dedicated GPUs for inference. We'll show networking diagrams with peering/TGW and the recommended ports.
[04:36] [Crosstalk] Jamal: When you say control plane in Aurora VPC is that something we manage?
[04:40] Priya: In the Private model, the customer can run a customer-managed control plane or use Redwood's managed control plane that is deployed into the customer's VPC (depending on contract). We'll note both options.
[04:49] Anika: For the marketplace deploy template -- do you support terraform modules that create all infra (VPC, subnets, security groups)?
[04:56] Dylan: Yes, our terraform module scaffolds VPC, SGs, IAM roles and deploys the helm chart. We'll make it parameterized for BYOK and SAML endpoints.
[05:07] Maya: Excellent. On the integration test run week of 12/27 -- what's the plan for benchmarks?
[05:13] Evan: We propose Redwood runs a small benchmark with a 2k token seq on a medium-sized LLM + q4_0 quantization and shares latency P50/P95 and token-cost estimates. Aurora can replicate the test in their environment with our terraform and helm snippet.
[05:29] Jamal: We'll need a reproducible test script and a sample corpus. Also a small cost estimate for running the benchmark -- do you have ballpark GPU hours?
[05:38] Priya: For the sample run, 4 hours on a single A10-equivalent should be fine to generate stable numbers. We'll include a script and an example dataset.
[05:48] Victor: Security-wise, during the benchmark we need secrets handled securely -- will Redwood's scripts fetch keys from Aurora KMS?
[05:55] Priya: Yes, the terraform/helm flow supports pulling secrets from KMS or referencing Kubernetes secrets that are created from KMS-backed values. We'll document steps.
[06:04] Anika: One more marketplace question -- do you have a standard checklist for listing partners? Things like support SLAs, EULA, pricing options?
[06:12] Evan: We do. We'll share a partner marketplace checklist that covers support tiers, SLAs, pricing models (consumption vs reserved dedicated), and required legal attachments.
[06:22] Maya: Great. Any concerns from Redwood about Aurora's marketplace policies?
[06:26] Evan: No major ones; mostly just clarity on deploy templates and how we surface billing. We prefer being able to show both hosted and dedicated pricing on the tile or link to a pricing page.
[06:38] Jonas: [misattributed, brief chuckle] Sorry, wrong call-- disregard.
[06:42] Priya: Back to ref arch -- I'll call out a couple of patterns: prefix caching (KV cache) to reduce repeated token costs, batching controls for low-latency apps, and autoscale settings for bursty traffic. Those are configuration knobs we recommend in the document.
[06:58] Jamal: For private on-prem customers, do you support offline air-gapped installs?
[07:03] Dylan: Yes we have an on-prem bundle. It's heavier but we provide an air-gapped install path and offline license keys. We'll include a reference note.
[07:12] Anika: Ok timeline recap?
[07:14] Evan: Action items -- Redwood to share draft ref arch by 12/20, Aurora to share security checklist by 12/15, Anika to provide marketplace assets by 12/18, and Redwood + Aurora to schedule bench run week of 12/27.
[07:30] Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[07:32] Victor: Nothing immediate. We'll review the security checklist and flag anything unusual.
[07:36] Evan: Perfect. We'll also put together a small repo for the demo with terraform/helm examples and attach it to the ref arch doc.
[07:44] Priya: I'll also add sample SAML and SCIM snippets.
[07:48] [Wrap-up] Evan: Cool thanks everyone. We'll send notes and the links. Next meeting -- follow-up after ref arch draft and after benchmark run, probably early January.
[07:59] Maya: Thanks all.

References/Links mentioned:
- Draft repo (placeholder): https://github.com/redwood-inference/aurora-integration (will share access)
- Ref arch doc (to be shared): https://redwood.ai/docs/refarch-aurora (draft)
- Marketplace checklist: https://redwood.ai/partner-marketplace-checklist (internal)

End of transcript.
